blocks.text: Pitt Meadows 55+ Condos: streets and boundaries

items.t: Pitt Meadows condos cluster along Harris Road and Lougheed Highway in the urban south of the city, inside a municipality where designated Agricultural Land Reserve land covers most of the ground outside that urban core, with the Pitt River to the west and the Fraser River to the south.

The City's Official Community Plan is Bylaw No. 2864, 2020, amended by Bylaw No. 3034, 2025 to add Small-Scale, Multi-Unit Housing as-of-right and to designate Transit-Oriented Areas beside the Pitt Meadows and Maple Meadows West Coast Express stations.

blocks.text: Pitt Meadows 55+ Condos: the housing stock

items.t: A named seniors residence a condo buyer should not confuse with ownership is The Wesbrooke at 12000 190A Street, a seniors living residence beside the Pitt Meadows Recreation Centre at 12027 Harris Road, which is rental and care product, not a strata condo you can buy.

New affordable rental supply is not condo supply either: Heron's Nest at 19085-119B Avenue is 115 affordable rental homes on City-owned land leased to Metro Vancouver Housing, and the 40 Katzie First Nation homes at 19676, 19679 and 19696 Salish Road are for Katzie members, completed December 2025.

blocks.text: Pitt Meadows 55+ Condos: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Provincial housing legislation now requires Small-Scale, Multi-Unit Housing as-of-right in Pitt Meadows urban neighbourhoods and Transit-Oriented Area designation beside the two West Coast Express stations, per the City's own 2025 Official Community Plan amendment, so the ground around a condo can densify without a site-by-site rezoning fight.

The City's plan work flags the seniors need directly: residents aged 65 and over are projected to roughly double, and those aged 85 and over to more than triple, with age-friendly, adaptable, single-level living named as the housing response the City wants.

blocks.text: Pitt Meadows 55+ Condos: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Pitt Meadows taxes were the region's lowest on the City's own comparison: the 2026 tax insert states that in 2025 Pitt Meadows had the lowest property taxes in the region at $5,002 for the average single-family home, and the second lowest combined with utility fees at $6,721.

Most of the city's land is farm-designated: the same insert charts designated Agricultural Land Reserve land at 78% for Pitt Meadows, the highest share shown, which is why condo supply stays inside a small urban footprint.

Utility fees in Pitt Meadows cover water, drainage, diking, sewer, solid waste and green waste as City services in the combined bill, so diking is a line item a condo owner pays even in an apartment building.

The City is actively redesigning its main street: the Harris Road Complete Street feasibility study was completed in 2025, covering a multi-use path, the Harris and Hammond intersection and protected bike lanes, to guide future capital work a Harris Road condo owner will live through.

Seniors services sit at the civic core: Pitt Meadows Recreation Centre at 12027 Harris Road hosts seniors recreation beside The Wesbrooke residence, so the Harris Road condo cluster is the walkable seniors-services cluster in this city.

blocks.text: Pitt Meadows 55+ Condos: development and new projects

items.t: Heron's Nest, 19085-119B Avenue: 115 affordable rental homes plus a child care centre for 150 children, on City-owned land leased to Metro Vancouver Housing Corporation with provincial funding through British Columbia Housing.

Katzie First Nation homes, 19676, 19679 and 19696 Salish Road: 40 affordable and supportive homes in three buildings, including 14 independent affordable homes for Elders and families, built with Katzie First Nation Affordable Housing Development Society, Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation and British Columbia Housing. Status: completed December 2025 and occupied, announced March 24, 2026 (as of November 3, 2026).
Status: plan adopted September 29, 2026 by Bylaw No. 3060, 2026 (as of November 3, 2026); individual projects still require further approvals.
Harris Road grade separation: City advocacy to separate road and rail traffic at Harris Road continues, with the City stating the aim is faster, safer commutes and better emergency response.

blocks.text: Pitt Meadows 55+ Condos: costs and taxes

items.t: Utility fees are inside the property tax bill in Pitt Meadows, received annually in June, covering water, drainage, diking, sewer and waste, so a condo buyer budgets tax and utilities as one City charge plus strata fees.

Commuter rail is the anchor: the West Coast Express serves Pitt Meadows station, and the City designates Transit-Oriented Areas beside it and Maple Meadows station, which is how the City itself frames condo transit access.

Lougheed Highway and Harris Road are the road spine, and the proposed 2-kilometre North Lougheed Connector would link Abernathy Way to Lougheed Highway to calm traffic on Old Dewdney Trunk Road, per the adopted area plan.

blocks.text: Pitt Meadows 55+ Condos: risks and due diligence

items.t: Diking and drainage are a standing cost and a standing risk: the City's utility list includes diking and drainage as core services in a floodplain city between two rivers, so a ground-level condo buyer should ask the strata about flood insurance and drainage work, not just the building envelope.

Rail noise and blockage are mapped by the City's own work: Harris Road rail-crossing monitoring and the grade-separation project exist because Canadian Pacific Kansas City trains block and sound through the Harris Road corridor beside the condo cluster.

Agricultural Land Reserve edges matter: with 78% of the city designated as reserve land on the City's chart, a condo on the urban edge can sit beside working farm land, with farm noise, spraying and restricted neighbouring development as normal conditions.

faq.a: The 55+ product here is rancher townhouses in Central Meadows and rental or care residences such as The Wesbrooke at 12000 190A Street, so a buyer set on a condo apartment should confirm any claimed age bylaw in the specific strata's filed bylaws before relying on it.
faq.q: Is there a true 55+ condo building in Pitt Meadows?

faq.a: Pitt Meadows sends one combined bill. The City collects property taxes and utility fees in a single annual bill, and its 2026 insert states the average single-family home was assessed at $1,184,823 with a total property tax and utility increase of $319 for 2026.
faq.q: Why do taxes and utilities arrive together here?
